title: Integral cubical lattice chains retract onto the augmentation
statement:
For an integer $r\geq0$ put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, with standard basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. For $0\leq a\leq r$ let $C_a$ be the free abelian group [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on symbols $[v,I]$ with $v\in D$ and $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $a$, and put $C_a=0$ otherwise. Define
$$\partial_a[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}\bigl([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}]\bigr),\qquad a\geq1.$$
Let $\epsilon:C_0\to\mathbf Z$ send every $[v,\varnothing]$ to $1$, let $s:\mathbf Z\to C_0$ send $1$ to $[0,\varnothing]$, and let $e:C_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ equal $s\epsilon$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Then $\partial_{a-1}\partial_a=0$, $\epsilon\partial_1=0$, and there are abelian-group homomorphisms $h_a:C_a\to C_{a+1}$ with
$$\partial_{a+1}h_a+h_{a-1}\partial_a=1-e_a\quad(a\geq0),\qquad \epsilon s=1,$$
where $h_{-1}\partial_0=0$. In particular $C_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathbf Z$ is exact as an augmented chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Translation $w[v,I]=[v+w,I]$ commutes with $\partial$ and $\epsilon$ (with trivial action on $\mathbf Z$); each $C_a$ is a finite direct sum of copies of the free integral $D$-module on $D$, one for each $I$ of size $a$. The maps $h_a$ and $s$ need not commute with translation. For $r=0$ take $s=\epsilon=1$ and $h=0$.
